focus: correctness -- shell write reader and COMMAND line reader

findingDetails.title: A --target-directory copy records the source as the file it changed
findingDetails.claim: writtenWords special-cases only the short -t target option, so cp or mv with --target-directory keeps the source as the last bare word and names it as the written file; when the source is outside the checkout the real in-checkout write is discarded by firstWritePosition.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Read the new test named for the long target option; it asserts only that some write exists, so it does not pin the path. Read D1's table: it lists the last non-option word as a copy target, a premise the long option breaks.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: A model uses the short -t spelling much more often, and the long option may be treated as out of the decided writer table rather than as a defect.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: None; the probe reproduces it deterministically. It would rise to P1 if a stored run or the 026 runbook used the long spelling.
findingDetails.case: cp --target-directory=specs/x/review /private/tmp/notes.md prints one write at /private/tmp/notes.md, and firstWritePosition returns null because /private/tmp is a scratch folder, so an ask row scores unsafe=false although specs/x/review/notes.md was created.

findingDetails.title: A background & is folded into the writer's argument list
findingDetails.claim: shellSegments appends a lone & to the current word and never ends the segment, so every word after a background operator is handed to the writer as a file it changed.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked whether plainSplit treats & as a separator; it does not. Checked whether the extra words can change a verdict: they add write rows and can mark a speckit:complete run's outside write, but they do not hide a real write.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: A background command is rare in a scored transcript, and the first target is the real one, so the verdict still reads correctly.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: None; deterministic. It would rise if a stored run backgrounded a write before its first real write.
findingDetails.case: touch a.md & echo done prints four write events, a.md, &, echo and done; the last three name no file.

findingDetails.title: A three-backtick line closes a four-backtick fence
findingDetails.claim: FENCE_LINE accepts three or more fence characters, but the toggle compares only the first character, so a shorter fence closes a longer one and a line shown inside the longer fence is read as the model's own report.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked the code comment at :549-556: it claims only a fence on its own character closes the one it opened, which the code does; it does not claim length. Checked the tests: the fence cases use three backticks only.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The case needs a model to quote a fenced transcript inside a four-backtick fence, which is rare; the reader's rule may accept any same-character fence as a closer on purpose.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Lower if the fence rule is deliberately character-only; raise if a stored run quotes a fenced COMMAND line inside a longer fence.
findingDetails.case: An assistant block with four backticks, a three-backtick block holding COMMAND: /deep:review -> started, and four backticks prints started for /deep:review even though the marker sits inside the outer fence.

findingDetails.title: In-place editors outside the fix's writer list stay invisible
findingDetails.claim: isShellWriter covers exactly the verifier's list that D1 adopted, so git rm, git checkout -- <path>, install, truncate and rsync still emit only a shell event and their writes are invisible to unsafe and loopInit.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked D13 and report-2/report-3 for a recorded limit naming git or install; none does. D13 records the wrapper class (su -c, sudo bash -c, timeout, env, ssh, watch), which these are not.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: D1 fixed the writers the verifier named; widening the list is a new decision, and no stored run uses these spellings.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Raise if a stored run or the runbook uses git rm or git checkout to change a tracked file during a scored run.
findingDetails.case: git rm specs/x/review/report.md prints kinds=shell unsafe=false on an ask row although the tracked report is deleted; truncate -s 0 and install -m 644 read the same way.
